title_en: This Popular and Nostalgic CD Player Art Frame I Found on Kickstarter Has Already Raised Over Half a Million Dollars From Backers, and You Could Still Be One of Them
summary_en: Time to bust out my CD binder.
body_en:
As part of IGN Finds, we are sharing cool things we find across the internet that we actually like, whether it be the latest LEGO idea, upcoming fandom merch or TCG drops, gaming preorders or the biggest tech deals.
One of the latest items on my radar this month is this SYITREN RM1: Frame Your Music, A Living Art CD Player , found on Kickstarter. There are thousands of Kickstarter projects popping up every month, but it's not often I see one that hits both music and 90s' nostalgia.
If you're old cool enough to have had any CD player growing up, then you get the appeal here. This takes me back to the simpler days in the 1990s and early 2000s, loading up my clunky six-disc CD player with the latest pop album, Now That's What I Call Music release, burned CD mixes, and movie soundtracks like Shrek and Grease. I'll admit I didn't think I'd see the day where I would want to put my CDs on display, or listen to them anywhere besides in my car, but here we are. It's time to bust out my CD binder again.
We first spotted this CD Player last month, and were impressed by its slick design and versatility. Since we posted this Tweet in early August, the Kickstarter is now at $543,895 from over 4,500 backers and counting.
This is one of the coolest Kickstarters I've seen in a while, a transparent CD player that looks like a piece of art you can hang up in your living room. It's already at $121,472, far exceeding its $3,000 initial goal with 26 days remaining. https://t.co/CbHuMH638a #ad https://t.co/Uz83YlhgLS
This Kickstarter has met its initial goal, but it's still offering late pledges which can give backers to up 55% off in rewards . Something to note is Kickstarter rewards aren’t guaranteed, so you’re supporting a creative project without guaranteed fulfillment. When you land on the Kickstarter page, you’ll see what available rewards are still available now, including the main options below (in order of popularity). The product(s) ship anywhere in the world with an estimated delivery of next month, October 2026.
This CD Player can be mounted on the wall, or on display via detachable stands on any shelf, table or desk. It includes transparent, dual-layer acrylic and precision metal pillars, showing the CD spin. It also displays light throughout the frame, via a warm yellow 2x8 LED matrix.
For the actual audio, you can pledge to get the RM1’s speaker with the CD player as part of the bundle. Or, you can use your own speaker, as this RM1 CD player uses Bluetooth 5.3 and connects to standard Bluetooth speakers (within approximately 10 meters). Playback starts automatically once a CD is loaded, with volume and skip buttons controlled via a remote. You can find out more product details on the Kickstarter campaign FAQ tab .
I'm not sure how long the late pledges will last, but if you missed the opportunity thus far, I'd jump on it. I'm personally a big fan of this music player and I think it would make an awesome holiday gift for a lot of people!
Lindsey (she/her) is IGN's Director of Audience Development and Commerce. She's been at IGN since 2021, spending the past nine years specializing in gaming, entertainment and tech in the publishing space, with a background in digital marketing. As she grew up thrift shopping her whole life, you may find her covering home and apparel deals from time to time, and checking out what's new from the world of queer TV and cinema.
